Both patches stop leaking the dup'd fds behind the GC-delayed close. A also fixes the shared socket: its map entry is a separate kept-open duplicate that is closed only when the last holder releases it. In B, closing the newest holder first (for example when a failed reload is rolled back) leaves the map pointing at a closed listener, so the next reuse of that path fails even though another holder is still live.

Both patches close the leaked dup fds, prevent double releases and protect abstract names, but Patch A still copies the fd from whichever holder was registered most recently: if that holder closes first, as when a failed reload leaves the old holder running, a later reuse fails. Patch B keeps a dedicated duplicate fd until the last holder closes, so the socket stays reusable in any close order, and its test also checks that the remaining holder still accepts connections.
